mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes ML 250 BlueTEC or 350 BlueTEC engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM651 engine for the ML 250 BlueTEC costs £2,500-£3,500 supply-only; a rebuilt OM642 engine for the ML 350 BlueTEC costs £3,500-£4,800 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - BlueTEC emissions systems require specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain gasket failure on a Mercedes ML 250 BlueTEC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oil leaks from around the chain tensioner gasket area are the classic warning sign on the OM651 engine. Mercedes issued a recall for 2015 ML 250 BlueTEC models over this issue. Leaking oil may drip onto a hot engine surface, increasing fire risk.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes ML 350 BlueTEC V6 engine (OM642) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 is a fundamentally strong engine, but BlueTEC variants face emissions system challenges. DPF, AdBlue, and EGR system issues are common, with owners reporting persistent check engine lights. Oil cooler seal degradation is also a known weakness.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes ML 250 BlueTEC and 350 BlueTEC engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM651 and OM642 BlueTEC engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. However, BlueTEC emissions components (AdBlue, DPF, EGR) may require attention from 60,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes ML 250 BlueTEC or 350 BlueTEC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the M Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt OM651 costs £2,500-£3,500 - far less than replacing an £8,000-£20,000 vehicle. The ML 350 BlueTEC's higher value (£10,000-£20,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes ML 250 BlueTEC or 350 BlueTEC need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 or 229.52 - typically 5W-30. The OM651 requires approximately 6.5 litres; the OM642 V6 requires approximately 8.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz M Class 250 BlueTEC/350 BlueTEC - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The ML 250 BlueTEC and ML 350 BlueTEC launched with the W166 generation in 2011, representing Mercedes' most advanced diesel technology at the time. The ML 250 BlueTEC introduced the OM651 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel - a high-efficiency engine already proven in the S-Class - while the ML 350 BlueTEC continued with the refined OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel. Both variants featured BlueTEC emissions technology with AdBlue SCR systems for Euro 6 compliance, making them some of the cleanest diesel SUVs of their era.

milestones.description: OM651.960, 2.1L four-cylinder BlueTEC diesel, 204hp (ML 250 BlueTEC, W166 launch)
OM642.826, 3.0L V6 BlueTEC diesel, 258hp (ML 350 BlueTEC, W166 launch)
2015 - Both variants continue with 9G-TRONIC transmission introduced on facelift models
M-Class rebranded to GLE; BlueTEC variants continue under GLE nameplate

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz M Class 250 BlueTEC/350 BlueTEC Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The M Class 250 BlueTEC's OM651 four-cylinder and the 350 BlueTEC's OM642 V6 are advanced Euro 6 diesel engines, but both have well-documented issues that drive replacement enquiries. The OM651 suffers from timing chain tensioner gasket oil leaks and fuel pump control unit failures, while the OM642 V6 is prone to oil cooler seal degradation and AdBlue system faults. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.
